content: Dr. Pat Simmons, born on November 21, 1974, in Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan, is a Canadian curler. He served as the skip for Team Saskatchewan in four consecutive Brier tournaments from 2005 to 2008. In 2005, Simmons earned his first appearance at the Brier after securing his inaugural provincial championship title. During that tournament, he led Saskatchewan to a 6-5 record, resulting in a four-way tie for fifth place, which left the team out of playoff contention. The following year, in 2006, Simmons once again skipped Saskatchewan at the Brier. However, the team concluded the event with a 5-6 record, tying for eighth place and failing to qualify for the playoffs. In 2007, Simmons demonstrated improved performance, guiding Saskatchewan to a 7-4 record. Despite this progress, the team narrowly missed the playoffs, finishing in fifth place. Finally, in 2008, Simmons achieved a significant milestone by leading Saskatchewan to a playoff position at the Brier. The team completed the round-robin stage with an impressive 9-2 record, securing second place. However, their playoff run ended in the semi-final, where they were defeated in an extra end by Ontario, skipped by Glenn Howard.
